blocks.text: English

按用户 id、筛选条件加载数据时，难的不是发请求，而是请求之外的事：慢的旧请求晚返回，把新结果盖掉；离开页面后请求还在跑；刷新时内容先清空再出现。`@migaia/resource` 把这些交给一个 `Resource`：你只写怎样取数据，它负责只保留最新的结果、取消过时的请求、缓存、重试和服务端渲染快照。它建立在 `@migaia/reactive` 之上，本身不发请求，用 `fetch`、RPC 还是数据库客户端由你决定。

离开页面后请求还在跑：报表还没加载完用户就走了，请求照样跑完，结果写进已经不存在的界面。根因是没有人在离开时取消请求，或者取消代码散在每个页面里。

blocks.text: 全部签名、边界行为与错误码见 USEGUIDE.md。下面是使用时最需要记住的约束。

1. 依赖追踪只认第一个 `await` 之前的同步读取。 `await` 之后再读响应式值不会被追踪；需要时先把值读进局部变量，或者把读取挪进一个 `Computed`。 2. 请求函数要把 `signal` 交给真正可取消的 I/O（例如 `fetch(url, { signal })`）。否则取消只是让 `Resource` 忽略这次结果，底层请求仍会跑完。 3. `refetch()` 总是发起新请求；被动读取（`state`、`promise`、`read()`）只在 `idle` 或数据过期时才发起。 想强制刷新就调用 `refetch()` 或 `invalidate()`。 4. 不再使用时要调用 `dispose()`，否则依赖登记和进行中的请求会一直留着。释放后读取数据和发起请求都抛 `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`；`disposed`、`refreshing`、`observed` 仍可读，`markDirty()`、`onDependencyDisconnected()` 和再次 `dispose()` 是安全的空操作。`dispose()` 不会释放传入的 `runtime`。 5. 默认 `keepAlive: false`。 没人读取 `state` 时，`Resource` 会和上游断开但保留依赖版本与缓存；下次读取时依赖没变且缓存有效就复用原值和 Promise，依赖变了就重新请求。需要“没人看也保持连接”时传 `keepAlive: true`。 6. `cancel()` 之后被动读取不会自动重启。 正在加载的请求被取消后状态是 `cancelled`；后台刷新被取消时保留旧数据并清除 `refreshing`。只有显式 `refetch()` 会重新开始。

`Resource` 自己产生的错误带 `source === RESOURCE_SOURCE`（`@migaia/resource`）和 `ResourceErrorCode` 里的 `code`。已经有完整 `source`/`code` 的外部错误保持原样；没有分类的加载失败在重试结束后附加 `FETCH_FAILED`，原生错误保持原类型，不可修改的错误保留在 `cause` 链上。重试策略本身出错时附加 `INVALID_OPTION`，触发它的加载错误仍可从错误链找到。取消和释放产生的错误是原生 `DOMException`（`name === 'AbortError'`），按 `error.name` 判断即可。
同一次请求在所有 Suspense 等待阶段复用同一个 pending Promise。请求函数抛出的 thenable 完成后，经注入的 scheduler 以 0ms 任务继续执行；Suspense 等待不计入重试次数，也没有次数上限。即使请求函数连续抛出立即完成的 thenable，取消任务仍能插进来执行，`cancel()`/`dispose()` 会停止后续调用。

`peekState()` 读取状态联合，不登记依赖、不发起请求、不检查有效期；和 `peek()` 不同，它返回状态对象而不是取值或抛出。`reset()` 取消当前请求、清除依赖和缓存，让同一个实例回到可复用的 `idle`；之前共享的 Promise 立即以原生 `AbortError`（`REQUEST_ABORTED`）失败。请求函数收到的 `IResourceFetchContext` 带只读的 `signal`、单调递增的 `generation` 和不透明的 `token`：同一次请求的多次重试共享它们，替换或重置后的新请求拿到新的一组。加载值的所有权和渲染版本租约由适配层负责，不属于 `Resource` 的依赖图。完整示例见 USEGUIDE。
`ResourceStatus.fetching` 已改为 `ResourceFetchStatus.fetching`；旧的 `IResourceStatus` / `IResourceFetchStatus` 类型改用与常量同名的 `ResourceStatus` / `ResourceFetchStatus` 键联合。运行时的状态字符串和后台刷新的数据、传输语义没有变化。
只在启动时加载一次、没有输入、不需要取消、重试或过期的数据（例如静态配置），直接 `await` 一个 Promise 更简单。

blocks.text: 页头、侧栏和设置页同时需要当前用户的资料。各自请求的话，同一份数据会同时发出三次。
常见的去重做法是把 Promise 存在模块变量里，可失败后由谁清除、过期后谁重新获取、页面离开时谁来取消，这些代码会散落在各个调用方。
同一个 `Resource` 的 `promise` 在请求进行中和缓存有效时都返回同一个 Promise。读取方只管 `await`，什么时候需要真正发请求由 `Resource` 决定。

`ttl` 默认是 `Infinity`：成功的数据会一直有效，直到依赖变化或调用 `refetch()`。共享只发生在同一个 `Resource` 实例内，参数不同的请求需要各自的实例。

blocks.text: 报表要 1 秒才加载完，用户中途离开了页面。请求还在跑，结果写进已经不存在的界面，或者一直占着连接和内存。
手写时要自己创建 `AbortController`，离开时调用 `abort()`，再在 `catch` 里区分“被取消”和“真失败”。每个页面都写一遍，漏掉一处就留下一个跑完才停的请求。
`dispose()` 会中止当前请求的 `signal`、清除依赖，并让还在等待的 `promise` 以 `AbortError` 失败。fetcher 只需要把 `signal` 交给底层请求。
输出：

blocks.code:
底层请求已停止
等待方收到：AbortError（REQUEST_ABORTED）
资源已释放：true

blocks.text: 调用 `dispose()` 后立即输出“底层请求已停止”，等待方收到 `AbortError`，错误码是 `REQUEST_ABORTED`。
`AbortError` 是原生的 `DOMException`，用 `error.name === 'AbortError'` 判断就能把它当作正常离开而不是故障。只想停掉这一次请求、之后还要复用资源时，改用 `cancel()`。

blocks.text: 用户点了“取消导出”，界面却弹出“导出失败”，因为取消和失败走进了同一个 `catch`。
手写的状态通常只有“加载中、成功、失败”三种，取消只能塞进“失败”，再靠比较错误信息字符串来区分。
`cancel()` 把还在等待的请求变成 `cancelled` 状态，`state.error` 是原生 `AbortError`。资源本身没有被释放，之后调用 `refetch()` 可以重新开始。
输出：

blocks.code:
状态：cancelled
原因：AbortError
第 2 次导出完成

blocks.text: 取消后状态是 `cancelled`，原因是 `AbortError`；随后 `refetch()` 正常完成，输出“第 2 次导出完成”。
`cancelled` 是单独的状态，界面可以按 `ResourceStatus.cancelled` 显示“已取消”。取消后再读取 `state` 不会自动重启请求，只有显式调用 `refetch()` 才会。

blocks.text: 价格表每次刷新都先清空成“加载中”，内容消失再出现，用户正在看的位置也跳走了。
手写时数据和加载状态通常放在同一个变量里，刷新就得先把数据清掉；要保留旧数据，就得再加一个“正在刷新”的标志，还要在每个出口记得复位。
开启 `staleWhileRevalidate` 后，刷新期间 `state` 保持 `success`，`data` 还是旧值，只多了 `refreshing: true`。新数据到了才替换。
输出：

blocks.code:

价格表 v1
价格表 v1（后台刷新中）
价格表 v2

blocks.text: 依次输出加载中、v1、v1（后台刷新中）、v2，刷新期间界面一直有内容。
`state.status` 描述屏幕上的数据；是否有请求在跑另看 `fetchStatus`（`ResourceFetchStatus`）。刷新被取消时，`refreshing` 会被清除，旧数据保留。
网关偶尔返回 503，重试一次就好；但 404 再怎么重试也没用，只会拖慢报错。
手写重试循环时，很容易对所有错误一律重试，或者在重试耗尽后抛出一个新的包装错误，调用方再也认不出原来的 `HttpError`。
`retry` 可以是一个函数，按第几次失败和错误对象决定要不要再试；`retryDelay` 决定每次等多久。停止重试后，拒绝的仍是最后一次的原始错误，`Resource` 只在它上面附加 `code`。
输出：

blocks.code:
第 1 次请求：503
第 2 次请求：404
最终失败：HTTP 404，仍是 HttpError：true
错误码：FETCH_FAILED

blocks.text: 第 1 次 503 后等 20ms 重试，第 2 次 404 不再重试，直接失败。
最终错误仍是那个 `HttpError`（`instanceof` 为真），只是多了错误码 `FETCH_FAILED`。已经带有自己 `source` 和 `code` 的错误保持原样。

sections.id: 服务端已取到的数据浏览器不再请求
sections.heading: 服务端已取到的数据浏览器不再请求

blocks.text: 服务端渲染时已经请求过一次用户资料，页面到了浏览器又请求一遍。首屏先闪一下加载状态，接口也多承受了一倍请求。
手写时常把数据塞进页面，在客户端判断“有数据就不请求”，但数据还能有效多久通常没人记，结果要么永不刷新，要么马上重取。
`dehydrate()` 导出数据和两个时长：已经存在了多久（`ageMs`）、还能有效多久（`remainingTtlMs`）。浏览器把它作为 `initialSnapshot` 传入，`Resource` 用本地时钟接着计时，快照仍有效时不发请求。
输出：

blocks.code:
首屏直接显示：Ada
浏览器端请求次数：0

blocks.text: 浏览器端第一次读取 `state` 就是 `success`，fetcher 一次也没有被调用。
快照只记录时长，不记录服务端的绝对时间，所以两边时钟不一致也没关系。传输或存储花掉的时间由调用方自己从 `remainingTtlMs` 里扣除；`data` 必须能被 JSON 序列化。

import { Resource, type IResourceOptions } from '@migaia/resource'
import type { IRuntime } from '@migaia/reactive'

class Resource<T> implements IObserver, IDisposable {
  constructor(fetcher: IResourceFetcher<T>, runtime: IRuntime, options?: IResourceOptions<T>)

  readonly runtime: IRuntime
  debugName?: string
  readonly deps: ReadonlySet<IObservable>
  readonly depVersions: ReadonlyMap<IObservable, number>

  readonly state: IResourceState<T>
  readonly promise: Promise<T>
  readonly disposed: boolean
  readonly refreshing: boolean
  readonly fetchStatus: ResourceFetchStatus
  readonly isStale: boolean
  readonly observed: boolean

  read(): T
  peek(): T
  peekState(): IResourceState<T>
  reset(): void
  refetch(): Promise<T>
  invalidate(): Promise<T>
  cancel(): void
  dehydrate(): IResourceCacheSnapshot<T> | undefined
  hydrate(snapshot: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>): void
  dispose(): void

  // IObserver 接口成员：由 @migaia/reactive 的依赖图在内部调用，一般不需要手动调用
  markDirty(): void
  onDependencyDisconnected(): void
}

blocks.text: 响应式的可取消异步资源：构造时给一个 `fetcher`，它跟踪 `fetcher` 在首次 `await` 之前同步读取的响应式值作为依赖；依赖变化时自动发起新请求，只有最新一代请求的结果才会生效。

动态关系是 `userId → Resource → rendering effect`：fetcher 在返回 Promise 前同步读取 `userId.value`，Runtime 因而把 Resource 登记为 `userId` 的 observer；Effect 读取 `user.state`，又成为 Resource 内部状态 Signal 的 observer。`userId` 写入经 Reactive 的 idle/microtask 通道使 Resource 标脏，Resource abort 旧 generation、创建新 generation，状态变化再驱动 Effect 重跑。旧请求即使忽略 abort 并延迟返回，也会被 generation 校验拒绝写回。首次 `await` 之后的响应式读取不在同步追踪窗口内，不会形成这条自动刷新链。
`new Resource(fetcher, runtime, options?)`：

items: `fetcher: IResourceFetcher<T>`（必填）—— `({ signal }) => T | PromiseLike<T>`。
`runtime: IRuntime`（必填）—— 来自 `@migaia/reactive` 的 `createRuntime()`/`defaultRuntime`；决定该 `Resource` 归属哪张依赖图。
`options?: IResourceOptions<T>`（可选，见配置项）。
全部选项在构造时一次性快照并校验（读取每个字段本身失败——hostile getter——都会被转换成贴 `INVALID_OPTION` 码的 `TypeError`，而不是让异常从任意后续调用点冒出）。
若提供了 `initialSnapshot`，构造期会先 `hydrate()` 它；随后若 `autoStart`（默认 `true`）为真且（没有初始快照，或初始快照已过期），立即发起首次请求。
`state: IResourceState<T>` —— 响应式状态机快照（读取会登记依赖，并顺带检查有效期：数据已过期的 `success` 或 `idle` 状态会自动发起新请求）。已释放时抛 `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`。
`promise: Promise<T>` —— 当前请求或最新缓存值对应的共享 Promise；多个读取者拿到同一个 Promise，只在 `idle`/过期时才真正启动工作。没有可返回的 Promise 时抛 `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE`。
`disposed: boolean` —— 是否已 `dispose()`；释放后仍可安全读取；`refreshing`、`observed` 也可读。
`refreshing: boolean` —— 是否正在后台刷新（`staleWhileRevalidate: true` 且当前展示的仍是旧成功值时为真）；已释放时返回 `false`（不抛错）。
`fetchStatus: ResourceFetchStatus` —— 传输层状态，独立于可见的 data/error：`'fetching'` 或 `'idle'`。
`isStale: boolean` —— 当前缓存的成功值是否已超过 TTL；非 `success` 状态恒为 `false`。
`observed: boolean` —— 是否有响应式消费者正在观察本资源的 `state`。

blocks.code:
read(): T; // Suspense 兼容：success 返回值，pending 抛 Promise，error/cancelled 抛错误
peek(): T; // 与 read() 形状相同，但不建立依赖边，也不检查有效期、不发起请求

blocks.text: `read()` 按 React Suspense 期望的形状工作：成功返回缓存数据；`pending`/`idle` 抛出当前 `promise`；`error`/`cancelled` 抛出对应的错误对象。`peek()` 是它的非追踪版本，用于 `getSnapshot` 一类"读当前快照但不想加入别人追踪窗口"的场景，且不会顺手启动请求。合法的 `autoStart: false` 初始 idle 状态尚无 Promise，直接 `peek()` 会抛 `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE`；用 `peekState()` 检查状态或显式启动请求。

blocks.code:
refetch(): Promise<T>;    // 总是发起新请求，不复用新鲜缓存
invalidate(): Promise<T>; // 立即使缓存过期（expiresAt = 0）并发起新请求

blocks.text: 被动读取（`state`/`promise`/`read()`）只在过期或 `idle` 时才发起请求；想强制刷新必须显式调用 `refetch()` 或 `invalidate()`。

blocks.code: cancel(): void;

blocks.text: 只中止当前活跃的一代请求，资源本身仍可复用；没有活跃请求时为空操作；取消活跃请求后暂停被动重启，pending 的可见状态保持 cancelled，显式 `refetch()` 可重启。`pending` 状态下取消会把状态落到 `cancelled`（携带 `name === 'AbortError'` 的 `DOMException`，贴 `REQUEST_CANCELLED` 码）；`staleWhileRevalidate` 后台刷新被取消时会回退展示原有的 `success` 数据（清除 `refreshing` 标记，不会遗留"正在刷新但没有实际请求"的不一致状态）。取消期间的清理（timer/listener）若失败，会以贴 `CANCELLATION_CLEANUP_FAILED` 码的错误抛出（不影响状态已经收敛这一事实）。

blocks.code:
dehydrate(): IResourceCacheSnapshot<T> | undefined;
hydrate(snapshot: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>): void;

blocks.text: `dehydrate()`：非 `success` 时返回 `undefined`；否则原样保留业务 `data`，同时捕获非负时长 `ageMs` 与 `remainingTtlMs`。后者为 `null` 表示无时间过期（`ttl: 0` 或无限 TTL）。任意 `T` 不保证 JSON 可序列化，BigInt/循环对象仍由调用方处理。

`hydrate(snapshot)`：先验证 v2，再按接收端 scheduler.now() 重建内部时间戳，作废当前请求并清空依赖，恢复 `success`。剩余寿命从 hydration 继续计时；调用方若需计入传输/存储耗时，应把已知耗时加到 `ageMs`，并从有限的 `remainingTtlMs` 扣除（最低为 0）。两端无需共享单调时钟原点。格式不是 v2、时长为负/非有限（仅 remaining 允许 null），或重建时间戳溢出时抛 `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`；getter 失败保留 cause。旧 v1 绝对时间格式明确拒绝，应在知道旧时钟基准的地方转换，接收端不能猜测。

blocks.code: dispose(): void;

blocks.text: 彻底终结资源：中止在途请求（`GenerationController.dispose()`）、清理依赖登记、释放内部状态 `Signal`。幂等——二次调用是空操作。清理过程中若某一步失败，第一个失败原样抛出，后续失败的错误挂在其 `.errors` 数组上（不会因为一步失败就跳过其余清理步骤）。释放后数据读取/请求操作抛 `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`；`disposed`、`refreshing`、`observed` 仍可读，`markDirty()`、`onDependencyDisconnected()` 和再次 `dispose()` 不抛错。

函数式构建 `Resource`。`setup` 只同步执行一次，拿到 `{ runtime, scheduler, signal, debugName, onDispose }`，返回 fetcher；数据类型从 fetcher 推导。`options` 就是 `IResourceOptions` 加上可选的 `runtime`（默认 `@migaia/reactive` 的 `defaultRuntime`）。

items: `onDispose` 注册的清理在 `dispose()` 时按注册的逆序执行，`signal` 同时中止。
`setup` 抛错、返回值不是函数（`RESOURCE_SETUP_INVALID`）或选项非法时，先中止 `signal`、逆序执行已注册清理，再重抛原始错误；清理失败挂在 `errors` 上。
`setup` 返回后再调用 `onDispose` 会抛 `RESOURCE_SETUP_CLOSED`，避免泄漏。

blocks.text: 配合 `ConfigOwner.fromAsync` 得到配置资源：

blocks.code: const config = createResource(() => ({ signal }) => ConfigOwner.fromAsync(fetch(url, { signal }).then((r) => r.text())))

items: `mutate(next | (previous) => next)`：本地写入成功数据（乐观更新、推送），取代进行中的请求，重新开始 TTL，返回 `this`。函数类型的数据需要包在 updater 里。
`subscribe(listener)`：在响应式图之外接收状态，立即回调一次，之后每次变化回调；监听器异常通过 `runtime.reportError` 报告。返回幂等的取消函数，`dispose()` 时自动取消。
`select(selector)`：基于成功数据的派生 computed，非成功状态时为 `undefined`，随资源一起释放。
`[Symbol.dispose]()`：支持 `using resource = createResource(...)`。

blocks.code:
type IResourceOptions<T = unknown> = {
  debugName?: string
  ttl?: number // 默认 Infinity（永不过期，除非依赖变化/手动刷新）
  autoStart?: boolean // 默认 true
  staleWhileRevalidate?: boolean // 默认 false
  retry?: IResourceRetryPolicy // 默认 0（不重试）
  retryDelay?: number | ((failureCount: number, error: unknown) => number) // 默认 0
  keepAlive?: boolean // 默认 false
  initialSnapshot?: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>
  scheduler?: IScheduler // 默认 @migaia/utils/scheduler 的 systemScheduler
}

type IResourceRetryPolicy = number | ((failureCount: number, error: unknown) => boolean)

blocks.text: 逐项语义与校验：

items: `ttl?: number` —— 成功值的新鲜时长（毫秒）。`0` 与 `Infinity`（默认）表示永不因时间过期，只会因依赖变化/`refetch()`/`invalidate()` 而刷新。非 `Infinity` 时必须是有限非负数，否则抛贴 `INVALID_OPTION` 码的 `RangeError`；`updatedAt + ttl` 运算结果非有限（数值溢出）同样抛 `INVALID_OPTION`。
`autoStart?: boolean` —— 是否在构造函数内立即发起首次请求。默认 `true`。若同时提供了新鲜的 `initialSnapshot`，即使 `autoStart: true` 也不会立即再发一次请求。
`staleWhileRevalidate?: boolean` —— 默认 `false`。为 `true` 时，刷新期间继续展示旧的 `success` 数据（附带 `refreshing: true`），而不是回退到 `pending`。

`retry?: number | (failureCount, error) => boolean` —— 固定次数或自定义判断函数。数字必须是非负整数，否则抛 `INVALID_OPTION`。函数形式在每次失败后被调用一次，用第几次失败（从 1 开始）与错误对象决定是否重试；Suspense 抛出的 thenable 值不计入失败次数（`fetcher` 内部同步抛出一个 thenable 是被当作"需要等待后重跑"处理的，不是一次真实失败）。

`retryDelay?: number | (failureCount, error) => number` —— 固定延迟或按失败次数计算的函数，单位毫秒。数字必须是有限非负数；函数返回非数字时以原生 `TypeError`/`INVALID_OPTION` 拒绝；返回负数/非有限数字则为 `RangeError`/`INVALID_OPTION`。策略抛错或返回非法值时保留触发重试的 fetch 主因，原生策略 Error 尽量原样附码，已有外部身份不改写。
`keepAlive?: boolean` —— 默认 `false`：长时间无人观察 `state` 会在下一个 idle 时机自动休眠（断开上游边、保留依赖版本与缓存），下次读取核对版本；依赖未变且缓存新鲜时继续复用，变更时重拉。设为 `true` 时禁用自动休眠。
`initialSnapshot?: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>` —— SSR/持久化恢复用的初始成功快照；构造期即 `hydrate()`，格式非法抛 `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`（详见快照类型）。

`scheduler?: IScheduler`（`@migaia/utils/scheduler`）—— 时间域与排程来源：TTL/`updatedAt`/`expiresAt`/重试延迟全部走同一个调度器，默认 `@migaia/utils/scheduler` 的 `systemScheduler`（单调时钟）。传入的值必须满足 `{ now(): number; schedule(cb, delayMs): IScheduledTask }` 契约（内部用 `snapshotScheduler` 校验），否则抛 `INVALID_OPTION`；缺宿主能力时该 scheduler 在被调用时才 fail-fast，不会静默降级成微任务。

blocks.text: `IResourceState<T>` 是 `state`/`peek()` 底层的判别联合，五态：`idle`（尚未发起过请求）、`pending`（请求在途，无历史数据）、`success`（`data` 为最新成功值，`refreshing` 仅在 `staleWhileRevalidate` 后台刷新时为 `true`）、`error`（`error` 为最近一次失败原因）、`cancelled`（`error` 恒为 `name === 'AbortError'` 的 `DOMException`，`code === ResourceErrorCode.requestCancelled`）。`ResourceStatus` 只包含这五种数据状态；独立的 `ResourceFetchStatus` 常量与同名 key union 只包含 `idle/fetching`，供 `fetchStatus` 表示传输活动。

blocks.code: type IResourceFetcher<T> = (ctx: IResourceFetchContext) => T | PromiseLike<T>

blocks.text: `fetcher` 在首次 `await` 之前同步读取的响应式值（`Signal`/`Computed`，包括异步函数在首个 `await` 之前的同步代码）会被登记为依赖，依赖变化时合并触发一次新请求（同一批变化只重新拉取一次）。`await` 之后再读响应式值不会被自动追踪——JavaScript 的同步依赖收集上下文在 `await` 处已经退出；需要的话应把这部分读取挪进一个 `Computed`，或在 `await` 之前先读入局部变量。
`fetcher` 必须把 `ctx.signal` 转交给真正可取消的 I/O（如 `fetch(url, { signal })`），否则 `cancel()`/依赖变化引发的取消只是让 `Resource` 忽略这次结果，底层请求仍会在后台跑完（浪费网络资源、可能产生未观察的副作用）。

`fetcher` 同步抛出的值若探测为 thenable（Suspense 常见模式：抛出一个 Promise 让上层挂起），会被当作"等待后重跑"处理，不计入重试次数；探测其 `.then` 时若 getter 本身抛错，无法判定是否为 thenable，会以携带 `SUSPENSE_PROBE_FAILED` 码的 `AggregateError` reject（原始抛出值与 getter 异常都保留在 `.errors` 里）。
快照只携带时长，不携带发送端绝对时间。`remainingTtlMs: null` 表示无时间过期；仅时间元数据可直接 JSON 编码，业务 `data` 由调用方保证可序列化。详见 hydrate() 的传输耗时责任和 v1 迁移说明。

sections.id: 底层依赖-lifecycle-原语的使用方式
sections.heading: 底层依赖：lifecycle 原语的使用方式

blocks.text: `Resource` 内部直接组合 `@migaia/lifecycle` 与 `@migaia/reactive` 的原语，理解这层有助于诊断边界行为：

items: `createGenerationController()`（来自 `@migaia/lifecycle`）——每次发起请求都调用 `begin()` 开一代新请求；`refetch()`/`invalidate()`/依赖变化都会使旧一代失效（`supersede()`），只有 `isCurrent(token)` 为真的那一代结果才会写入 `state`。`dispose()` 时调用其 `dispose()` 终结控制器。
`createTerminalController()`（来自 `@migaia/lifecycle`）——驱动 `Resource` 自身的容器存活轴（`open → closing → terminal`）；`disposed` getter 直接读它的 `lifecycle === 'terminal'`。
`probeThenable()` / `assimilateCapturedThen()`（来自 `@migaia/utils/function`）——用于安全探测 `fetcher` 同步抛出的值是否是 thenable（Suspense 抛 Promise 模式），只读一次 `.then`，避免 hostile getter 被读取两次或异常被吞掉。
`systemScheduler`（来自 `@migaia/utils/scheduler`）/ `snapshotScheduler()`（来自 `@migaia/lifecycle`）——`scheduler` 选项的默认值与校验函数；TTL 到期判定、重试延迟计时都通过它，不直接使用宿主 `setTimeout`/`Date.now`。
`internalRuntimeOf()` / `createTrackedObserver()`（来自 `@migaia/reactive/extension`）——Resource作为IObserver接入图，仅获得绑定自身的追踪、挂起、重验证与idle能力；依赖集合由reactive内部维护，请求、取消与资源释放仍由Resource负责。

blocks.code: import { RESOURCE_SOURCE, ResourceErrorCode, type IResourceErrorCode } from '@migaia/resource'

blocks.text: 稳定错误码表，9 个码，唯一声明处 `src/error-code.ts`，包自身错误的 `source` 为 `'@migaia/resource'`；已有完整外部身份的错误保留原包身份。 `RESOURCE_SOURCE` 导出这个稳定 source，跨包分类错误时应比较它与 `ResourceErrorCode`，不要复制字符串字面量。

rows: 在已 `dispose()` 的 `Resource` 上调用任意读取/操作方法
请求停止时的原生 AbortError；Resource 主动取消时与 signal.reason 同一，lifecycle replacement reason 保留在 cause
调用方显式 `cancel()` 导致当前 pending 请求被取消，`state` 落入 `cancelled` 所携带的 `DOMException`
请求取消已完成状态收敛，但取消期间的 timer/listener cleanup 失败
读取 `promise`，或在 `pending`/`idle` 状态下调用 `read()`/`peek()` 时，没有正在进行或已缓存的 Promise 可返回
非 v2 快照、负/非有限时长（remaining 可为 null）、本地重建时间戳溢出或 getter 失败
构造/调用时传入的选项（`ttl`、`retry`、`retryDelay`、`scheduler` 等）不满足取值要求
`fetcher` 抛出用于 Suspense 的值，但探测其 `.then` 时 getter 本身抛错，无法判定是否为 thenable
重试耗尽后的未分类 fetch 失败；原生错误尽量保留身份，冻结错误/非 Error 值保留在 cause，已有外部身份不改写

blocks.text: `requestAborted`/`requestCancelled` 抛出/落入状态的值始终是原生 `DOMException`（`name === 'AbortError'`），调用方通常按 `error.name === 'AbortError'` 判定并静默处理，而不是当作真实失败；`code` 只作为附加字段挂上，不改变类型。调用方应始终以 `error.code === ResourceErrorCode.xxx` 判别，不要硬编码码值字符串。

blocks.code:
await resource.invalidate() // 立即视为过期并重新请求
resource.cancel() // 只中止当前请求，资源仍可复用；被动读取保持暂停，显式 refetch() 重启

items: 依赖变了但没有自动重新请求：检查响应式读取是否发生在 `fetcher` 的首次 `await` 之前；`await` 之后的读取不会被追踪，应挪进 `Computed` 或提前读入局部变量。
`cancel()`/依赖变化后底层请求似乎仍在跑：`fetcher` 没有把 `ctx.signal` 转交给真正可取消的 I/O；`cancel()` 只是让 `Resource` 忽略这次结果，不会代为中止未接收 `signal` 的请求。
重复读 `state`/`promise` 却拿不到最新数据：被动读取只在过期或 `idle` 时才发起请求，重复读不会强制刷新；需要强制刷新用 `refetch()` 或 `invalidate()`。
读取抛 `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`：`Resource` 已被 `dispose()`；停止持有该引用，创建新的 `Resource` 实例。
读取抛 `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE`：合法的 `autoStart: false` idle 上直接 `peek()` 也会触发；用 `peekState()` 检查状态，或用 `promise`/`refetch()` 启动工作。
`hydrate()`/`initialSnapshot` 抛 `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`：快照通常来自 SSR 序列化或持久化存储，格式漂移应在装载时就失败；检查快照的产出/序列化路径，确认 `version === 2`、`ageMs` 为有限非负数、`remainingTtlMs` 为有限非负数或 null。

blocks.text: `peekState()` 返回当前的 `IResourceState<T>`，不登记依赖、不发起加载，也不检查有效期。和 `peek()` 不同，它返回状态联合本身，而不是取出值或抛出。`reset()` 取消进行中的请求，清除依赖和缓存数据，让同一个实例回到可复用的 `idle`。之前那个 pending Promise 立即以原生 `AbortError` 失败，`source` 为 `@migaia/resource`，`code` 为 `REQUEST_ABORTED`；重置后的请求不会沿用旧的 generation 或 token。

blocks.text: 中文

When data depends on a user id or a set of filters, sending the request is the easy part. The hard part is everything around it: a slow old request answers late and overwrites the new result, a request keeps running after the user leaves, a refresh blanks the content before showing it again. `@migaia/resource` gives all of that to one `Resource`. You write how to load the data; it keeps only the newest result, cancels outdated requests, caches, retries and produces server-rendering snapshots. It is built on `@migaia/reactive` and sends no requests itself: `fetch`, RPC or a database client is your choice.

items: An old result overwrites the new one: the user types `re`, then completes it to `react`; the `re` request is slower, and the page ends up showing the results for `re`. The cause is that every request writes its result when it answers, so whichever answers last wins.

A request keeps running after the user leaves: the report has not finished loading when the user moves on, the request runs to the end anyway and writes into a view that no longer exists. The cause is that nobody cancels the request on leaving, or the cancelling code is repeated on every page.

The content flashes on refresh: every refresh of the price list blanks it to "loading" before it comes back. The cause is that data and loading state share one variable, so refreshing has to clear the data first.

Retries without judgement: a 404 is retried too, and afterwards a new wrapper error is thrown, so the caller can no longer recognize its own `HttpError`. The cause is a retry loop that neither tells errors apart nor keeps the original one.

The browser loads again what the server already loaded: server rendering fetched the user profile, and the browser fetches it again as soon as the page arrives, so the first screen flashes a loading state. The cause is that the data reached the browser but how long it stays valid did not.

An old request cannot write its result, even when the API cannot be cancelled. By hand, whichever answers last wins; `Resource` gives every request a generation number and writes only the newest generation's result to `state`. Example

Dependencies are recorded for you, and several changes in one turn send one request. By hand, each filter's change handler sends its own request; every reactive value the fetcher reads before its first `await` becomes a dependency, and several changes in the same turn merge into one request on the next microtask. Example

Every reader shares one Promise. Hand-written de-duplication has to clear the Promise after a failure and fetch again after expiry; the `promise` of one `Resource` returns the same Promise while a request runs and while the cache is fresh. Example

Cancellation has its own state and is never mistaken for a failure. After `cancel()` the state is `cancelled` and the resource can still `refetch()`; `dispose()` passes the abort on to the underlying request, and waiters receive a native `AbortError`. Example

Server snapshots carry the remaining lifetime, not a point in time. The browser keeps counting on its own clock, so the two clocks need not agree, and no request is sent while the snapshot is fresh. Example

blocks.text: A few terms:

items: Passive read: reading `state`, `promise` or `read()`. It starts a request only when nothing has been requested yet or the data has expired; reading again does not force a refresh.
Explicit refresh: `refetch()` always starts a new request; `invalidate()` expires the cache first and then requests.

Suspension: when nobody reads `state`, the `Resource` disconnects from its inputs but keeps the cache. The next read checks the inputs first and reuses the cache when they did not change and it has not expired.

blocks.text: Every signature, boundary behaviour and error code is in USEGUIDE.en.md. These are the constraints that matter most in use.

1. Dependency tracking sees only synchronous reads before the first `await`. Reactive values read after an `await` are not tracked; read them into a local variable first, or move the read into a `Computed`. 2. The fetcher should hand `signal` to I/O that can really be cancelled (for example `fetch(url, { signal })`). Otherwise a cancel only makes the `Resource` ignore the result, and the underlying request still runs to the end. 3. `refetch()` always starts a new request; passive reads (`state`, `promise`, `read()`) start one only when idle or expired. Call `refetch()` or `invalidate()` to force a refresh. 4. Call `dispose()` when the resource is no longer used, or its dependency registrations and running request stay alive. After disposal, data reads and request operations throw `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`; `disposed`, `refreshing` and `observed` stay readable, and `markDirty()`, `onDependencyDisconnected()` and a second `dispose()` are safe no-ops. `dispose()` does not dispose the `runtime` passed in. 5. `keepAlive` defaults to `false`. When nobody reads `state`, the `Resource` disconnects from its upstream but keeps the dependency versions and the cache; the next read reuses the old value and Promise when the dependencies did not change and the cache is fresh, and requests again when they changed. Pass `keepAlive: true` to stay connected while nobody watches. 6. Passive reads do not restart after `cancel()`. A cancelled initial load is in the `cancelled` state; a cancelled background refresh keeps the old data and clears `refreshing`. Only an explicit `refetch()` starts again.

Errors produced by `Resource` itself carry `source === RESOURCE_SOURCE` (`@migaia/resource`) and a `code` from `ResourceErrorCode`. Foreign errors that already have a full `source`/`code` stay as they are; an unclassified load failure receives `FETCH_FAILED` once retrying ends, native errors keep their type, and immutable errors remain on the `cause` chain. A failing retry policy receives `INVALID_OPTION`, and the load error that triggered it stays reachable on the error chain. Errors produced by cancellation and disposal are native `DOMException`s (`name === 'AbortError'`), so checking `error.name` is enough.

One request reuses one pending Promise across every Suspense wait. After a thenable thrown by the fetcher settles, the work continues through a 0 ms task on the injected scheduler; Suspense waits do not count as retries and have no upper limit. Even when the fetcher keeps throwing thenables that settle at once, cancellation tasks can still run, and `cancel()`/`dispose()` stop further calls.

`peekState()` reads the state union without recording a dependency, starting a request or checking the lifetime; unlike `peek()`, it returns the state object instead of returning the value or throwing. `reset()` cancels the current request and clears the dependencies and the cache, bringing the same instance back to a reusable `idle`; the previously shared Promise rejects at once with a native `AbortError` (`REQUEST_ABORTED`). The `IResourceFetchContext` given to the fetcher carries a readonly `signal`, a monotonically increasing `generation` and an opaque `token`: retries of one request share them, and a replacement or reset request receives a new set. Ownership of loaded values and render-version leases belong to adapters, not to the `Resource` dependency graph. See the USEGUIDE for a complete example.

`ResourceStatus.fetching` became `ResourceFetchStatus.fetching`; the former `IResourceStatus` / `IResourceFetchStatus` types are replaced by the key unions `ResourceStatus` / `ResourceFetchStatus` that share their constants' names. The runtime status strings and the data and transport semantics of background refresh are unchanged.
For data loaded once at startup, with no inputs and no need for cancellation, retries or expiry (static configuration, for example), a plain `await` on a Promise is simpler.

sections.heading: Show only the result for the latest input

blocks.text: A search box receives `re`, then the user completes it to `react`. The `re` request is slower and answers after `react`, so the page ends up showing the results for `re`.

The usual code sends a request whenever the input changes and writes the result inside `then`. Every request writes, so whichever answers last wins; when the API cannot be cancelled, an `AbortController` cannot stop that write either.

`Resource` gives every request a generation number and writes only the newest generation's result to `state`. The fetcher reads `keyword.value` before its first `await`, so a keyword change starts a new request without any extra listener.
Output:

blocks.code:
API answered: "react"
page shows: 3 results for "react"
API answered: "re"

blocks.text: `react` answers first and is shown. `re` answers 50 ms later; the log shows the API answering, but the page does not change again.
Even when the underlying request cannot be cancelled, a replaced request cannot write into `state`. When the API accepts a `signal`, pass it on to stop the network work as well.

sections.heading: Change several filters, send one request

blocks.text: Switching the sort order on a list page also moves the page number. If each change triggers its own request, one request is wasted and discarded, the API takes twice the load, and the loading state flashes twice.
Hand-written code usually sends a request from each filter's change handler. Merging them means adding a debounce, and the right debounce delay is hard to pick.
`Resource` records both `page` and `sort` as dependencies because the fetcher reads them. Several writes in the same turn only mark it stale, and the next microtask turns them into one request.
Output:

blocks.code:
request: page 1, sorted by newest
shows: orders for page 1, sorted by newest
request: page 2, sorted by popular
shows: orders for page 2, sorted by popular

blocks.text: After the first request, changing the sort order and the page together adds exactly one line: `request: page 2, sorted by popular`.
The two writes became one request that reads the final value of both filters; no request for "page 1, popular" is ever sent.
The header, the sidebar and the settings page all need the current user's profile at once. If each asks on its own, the same data is requested three times in parallel.

The common fix is to keep the Promise in a module variable, but then someone has to clear it after a failure, fetch again after it expires and cancel it when the page goes away, and that code ends up spread over every caller.

The `promise` of one `Resource` returns the same Promise while a request is running and while the cached value is fresh. Readers just `await` it; the `Resource` decides when a request is really needed.
Output:

blocks.code:
requests: 1
all three got the same object: true
requests after another read: 1

blocks.text: All three readers receive the same object and one request is sent; reading `promise` again later still finds a fresh cache, so the count stays at 1.

`ttl` defaults to `Infinity`: a success stays fresh until a dependency changes or `refetch()` runs. Sharing happens within one `Resource` instance; requests with different parameters need their own instances.

sections.heading: Stop the running request when the user leaves

blocks.text: A report takes a second to load and the user leaves halfway. The request keeps running, and its result is written into a view that no longer exists or keeps holding a connection and memory.

By hand you create an `AbortController`, call `abort()` when leaving, and tell "cancelled" apart from "really failed" in `catch`. Every page repeats this, and one missed place leaves a request that only stops when it finishes.
`dispose()` aborts the current request's `signal`, clears the dependencies and makes a pending `promise` fail with `AbortError`. The fetcher only has to hand `signal` to the underlying request.
Output:

blocks.code:
underlying request stopped
waiter received: AbortError (REQUEST_ABORTED)
resource disposed: true

blocks.text: Right after `dispose()` the log shows the underlying request stopping, and the waiter receives `AbortError` with code `REQUEST_ABORTED`.

`AbortError` is a native `DOMException`, so `error.name === 'AbortError'` is enough to treat it as a normal exit rather than a fault. To stop only this request and reuse the resource later, call `cancel()` instead.

sections.heading: Show cancelled instead of an error

blocks.text: The user clicks "Cancel export" and the page shows "Export failed", because cancellation and failure end up in the same `catch`.
Hand-written state usually has only loading, success and failure. Cancellation is squeezed into failure and told apart by comparing message strings.
`cancel()` turns the pending request into the `cancelled` state, with a native `AbortError` in `state.error`. The resource is not disposed; `refetch()` starts it again.
Output:

blocks.code:
status: cancelled
reason: AbortError
export 2 finished

blocks.text: After cancelling, the status is `cancelled` with reason `AbortError`; the following `refetch()` completes and prints `export 2 finished`.

`cancelled` is a state of its own, so the page can branch on `ResourceStatus.cancelled` to show "cancelled". Reading `state` after a cancel does not restart the request; only an explicit `refetch()` does.

sections.heading: Keep showing old data while refreshing

blocks.text: Every refresh of the price list first blanks it to "loading". The content disappears and comes back, and the reader loses their place.

Hand-written code usually keeps data and loading state in one variable, so refreshing means clearing the data first. Keeping the old data needs another "is refreshing" flag that every exit path must remember to reset.
With `staleWhileRevalidate`, `state` stays `success` during a refresh, `data` keeps the old value and only `refreshing: true` is added. The new data replaces it when it arrives.
Output:

blocks.code:
loading…
price list v1
price list v1 (refreshing in the background)
price list v2

blocks.text: The output is loading, v1, v1 refreshing in the background, then v2. The page always has content during the refresh.

`state.status` describes the data on screen; whether a request is running is reported separately by `fetchStatus` (`ResourceFetchStatus`). If the refresh is cancelled, `refreshing` is cleared and the old data stays.
A gateway sometimes answers 503 and a retry fixes it, but retrying a 404 never helps and only delays the error.
Hand-written retry loops easily retry every error, or throw a new wrapper error once retries run out, so the caller can no longer recognize its own `HttpError`.

`retry` can be a function that decides from the failure count and the error whether to try again, and `retryDelay` decides how long to wait. When retrying stops, the last original error is rejected; `Resource` only attaches a `code` to it.
Output:

blocks.code:
request 1: 503
request 2: 404
final failure: HTTP 404, still an HttpError: true
code: FETCH_FAILED

blocks.text: After the 503 the resource waits 20 ms and tries again; the 404 is not retried and the request fails.
The final error is still the same `HttpError` (`instanceof` is true) and now carries the code `FETCH_FAILED`. An error that already has its own `source` and `code` keeps them.

sections.heading: Do not request server-loaded data again

blocks.text: Server rendering already loaded the user profile, and the browser loads it again as soon as the page arrives. The first screen flashes a loading state and the API takes twice the requests.
Hand-written code often embeds the data in the page and skips the request when data is present, but nobody records how long that data stays valid, so it either never refreshes or refetches at once.

`dehydrate()` exports the data plus two durations: how old it is (`ageMs`) and how long it stays fresh (`remainingTtlMs`). The browser passes it as `initialSnapshot`; the `Resource` keeps counting on its own clock and sends no request while the snapshot is fresh.
Output:

blocks.code:
first paint shows: Ada
requests in the browser: 0

blocks.text: The first read of `state` in the browser is already `success`, and the fetcher was never called.

The snapshot carries durations, not the server's absolute time, so the two clocks need not agree. Time spent in transport or storage is the caller's to subtract from `remainingTtlMs`, and `data` must be JSON-serializable.

blocks.text: A reactive, cancellable async resource. You give it a `fetcher`; the reactive values the `fetcher` reads synchronously before its first `await` become dependencies. When a dependency changes a new request starts automatically, and only the newest generation's result takes effect.

The live chain is `userId → Resource → rendering effect`. The fetcher reads `userId.value` synchronously before returning its Promise, so the Runtime registers the Resource as an observer of `userId`; the effect reads `user.state` and becomes an observer of the Resource's internal state signal. A write to `userId` marks the Resource dirty through Reactive's idle/microtask channel; the Resource aborts the old generation and starts a new one, and the state change reruns the effect. Even when the old request ignores the abort and answers late, the generation check refuses to write it back. Reactive reads after the first `await` are outside the synchronous tracking window and do not create this refresh chain.
`new Resource(fetcher, runtime, options?)`:

items: `fetcher: IResourceFetcher<T>` (required): `({ signal }) => T | PromiseLike<T>`.
`runtime: IRuntime` (required): `createRuntime()` or `defaultRuntime` from `@migaia/reactive`; decides which dependency graph the `Resource` belongs to.
`options?: IResourceOptions<T>` (optional, see Options).

Every option is snapshotted and validated once in the constructor. A failure while reading a field itself (a hostile getter) becomes a `TypeError` with code `INVALID_OPTION`, instead of surfacing later from an arbitrary call.

When `initialSnapshot` is given, the constructor `hydrate()`s it first. Then, if `autoStart` (default `true`) is on and there is no initial snapshot or it has expired, the first request starts immediately.

`state: IResourceState<T>`: the reactive state-machine snapshot. Reading it records a dependency and checks the lifetime: an expired `success` or an `idle` state starts a new request. Throws `RESOURCE_DISPOSED` after disposal.

`promise: Promise<T>`: the shared Promise of the current request or the latest cached value. Every reader receives the same Promise, and work starts only when idle or expired. Throws `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE` when there is no Promise to return.
`disposed: boolean`: whether `dispose()` was called; safe to read after disposal, as are `refreshing` and `observed`.
`refreshing: boolean`: whether a background refresh is running (`staleWhileRevalidate: true` while the old success is still shown); returns `false` after disposal instead of throwing.
`fetchStatus: ResourceFetchStatus`: transport status, independent of the visible data/error: `'fetching'` or `'idle'`.
`isStale: boolean`: whether the cached success has passed its TTL; always `false` outside `success`.
`observed: boolean`: whether a reactive consumer currently observes this resource's `state`.

blocks.code:
read(): T; // Suspense-compatible: success returns the value, pending throws the Promise, error/cancelled throws the error
peek(): T; // same shape as read(), but records no dependency and neither checks the lifetime nor starts a request

blocks.text: `read()` follows the shape React Suspense expects: it returns the cached data on success, throws the current `promise` while `pending`/`idle`, and throws the error object for `error`/`cancelled`. `peek()` is its untracked version, for `getSnapshot`-style reads that must not join another consumer's tracking window, and it never starts a request. A legitimate `autoStart: false` idle state has no Promise yet, so calling `peek()` there throws `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE`; inspect with `peekState()` or start a request explicitly.

blocks.code:
refetch(): Promise<T>;    // always starts a new request, never reuses a fresh cache
invalidate(): Promise<T>; // expires the cache at once (expiresAt = 0) and starts a new request

blocks.text: Passive reads (`state`/`promise`/`read()`) start a request only when expired or `idle`; to force a refresh, call `refetch()` or `invalidate()`.

blocks.code: cancel(): void;

blocks.text: Stops only the currently active generation; the resource stays reusable. Without an active request it is a no-op. After cancelling an active request, passive restarts pause: a cancelled `pending` stays visible as `cancelled` until an explicit `refetch()`. Cancelling in `pending` moves the state to `cancelled`, carrying a `DOMException` with `name === 'AbortError'` and code `REQUEST_CANCELLED`. Cancelling a `staleWhileRevalidate` background refresh falls back to showing the existing `success` data and clears `refreshing`, so no "refreshing without a request" state is left behind. If cleanup during cancellation (timers/listeners) fails, it is thrown as an error with code `CANCELLATION_CLEANUP_FAILED`; the state has converged regardless.

blocks.code:
dehydrate(): IResourceCacheSnapshot<T> | undefined;
hydrate(snapshot: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>): void;

blocks.text: `dehydrate()` returns `undefined` outside `success`. Otherwise it keeps the business `data` as is and captures two non-negative durations, `ageMs` and `remainingTtlMs`; the latter is `null` when there is no time-based expiry (`ttl: 0` or an infinite TTL). An arbitrary `T` is not guaranteed to be JSON-serializable; BigInt and cyclic objects remain the caller's concern.

`hydrate(snapshot)` validates v2 first, rebuilds the internal timestamps from the receiving side's `scheduler.now()`, voids the current request, clears the dependencies and restores `success`. The remaining lifetime continues from the moment of hydration; to account for transport or storage time, add the known time to `ageMs` and subtract it from a finite `remainingTtlMs` (down to 0). The two sides need no shared monotonic clock origin. blocks.text: Ends the resource for good: aborts the running request (`GenerationController.dispose()`), clears the dependency registrations and releases the internal state signal. Idempotent: a second call is a no-op. If a cleanup step fails, the first failure is thrown as is and later failures are attached to its `.errors` array; one failing step never skips the remaining steps. type IResourceOptions<T = unknown> = {
  debugName?: string
  ttl?: number // default Infinity (never expires; only dependency changes or manual refreshes reload)
  autoStart?: boolean // default true
  staleWhileRevalidate?: boolean // default false
  retry?: IResourceRetryPolicy // default 0 (no retry)
  retryDelay?: number | ((failureCount: number, error: unknown) => number) // default 0
  keepAlive?: boolean // default false
  initialSnapshot?: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>
  scheduler?: IScheduler // default systemScheduler from @migaia/utils/scheduler
}

type IResourceRetryPolicy = number | ((failureCount: number, error: unknown) => boolean)

blocks.text: Semantics and validation, field by field:

items: `ttl?: number`: how long, in milliseconds, a success stays fresh. `0` and `Infinity` (the default) never expire by time; only dependency changes, `refetch()` or `invalidate()` reload. Other values must be finite and non-negative, otherwise a `RangeError` with code `INVALID_OPTION` is thrown; an `updatedAt + ttl` that is not finite (numeric overflow) also throws `INVALID_OPTION`.
`autoStart?: boolean`: whether the constructor starts the first request. Default `true`. With a fresh `initialSnapshot`, no request starts even when `autoStart` is `true`.
`staleWhileRevalidate?: boolean`: default `false`. When `true`, a refresh keeps showing the old `success` data (with `refreshing: true`) instead of falling back to `pending`.

`retry?: number | (failureCount, error) => boolean`: a fixed count or a decision function. A number must be a non-negative integer, otherwise `INVALID_OPTION`. The function is called once after each failure with the failure number (starting at 1) and the error, and decides whether to retry. Thenables thrown for Suspense do not count as failures: a fetcher that synchronously throws a thenable is treated as "wait, then run again", not as a real failure.

`retryDelay?: number | (failureCount, error) => number`: a fixed delay or a function of the failure count, in milliseconds. A number must be finite and non-negative. A function returning a non-number rejects with a native `TypeError` and `INVALID_OPTION`; a negative or non-finite number gives a `RangeError` with `INVALID_OPTION`. When the policy throws or returns an invalid value, the fetch error that triggered the retry stays reachable; native policy errors receive the code in place where possible, and existing foreign identities are not rewritten.

`keepAlive?: boolean`: default `false`. When nobody observes `state` for a while, the resource suspends at the next idle moment (disconnects upstream edges, keeps dependency versions and the cache); the next read checks the versions, reuses the cache when nothing changed and it is fresh, and reloads otherwise. `true` disables suspension.

`initialSnapshot?: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>`: the initial success snapshot for server rendering or persisted restore; it is `hydrate()`d in the constructor, and an invalid format throws `INVALID_SNAPSHOT` (see Snapshot type).

`scheduler?: IScheduler` (`@migaia/utils/scheduler`): the time and scheduling source. TTL, `updatedAt`, `expiresAt` and retry delays all go through this one scheduler; the default is `systemScheduler` from `@migaia/utils/scheduler` (a monotonic clock). The value must satisfy `{ now(): number; schedule(cb, delayMs): IScheduledTask }` (checked internally with `snapshotScheduler`), otherwise `INVALID_OPTION`. A scheduler missing a host capability fails fast when called instead of silently falling back to microtasks.

blocks.text: `IResourceState<T>` is the discriminated union behind `state`/`peek()`, with five states: `idle` (no request yet), `pending` (a request is running and there is no earlier data), `success` (`data` is the latest success; `refreshing` is `true` only during a `staleWhileRevalidate` background refresh), `error` (`error` is the latest failure) and `cancelled` (`error` is always a `DOMException` with `name === 'AbortError'` and `code === ResourceErrorCode.requestCancelled`). `ResourceStatus` contains only these five data states; the separate `ResourceFetchStatus` constant and its same-named key union contain only `idle/fetching`, for the transport activity reported by `fetchStatus`.

blocks.code: type IResourceFetcher<T> = (ctx: IResourceFetchContext) => T | PromiseLike<T>

blocks.text: Reactive values (`Signal`/`Computed`) the `fetcher` reads synchronously before its first `await`, including the synchronous part of an async function before its first `await`, become dependencies; a dependency change merges into one new request (one batch of changes reloads only once). Reactive values read after an `await` are not tracked, because JavaScript's synchronous tracking context has already ended there; move such reads into a `Computed`, or read them into local variables before awaiting.

The `fetcher` must hand `ctx.signal` to I/O that can really be cancelled (such as `fetch(url, { signal })`). Otherwise a `cancel()` or a dependency change only makes the `Resource` ignore the result, and the underlying request keeps running in the background, wasting network resources and possibly causing unobserved side effects.

When a value thrown synchronously by the `fetcher` is detected as a thenable (the common Suspense pattern: throw a Promise to suspend the caller), it is treated as "wait, then run again" and does not count as a retry. If reading its `.then` throws, the value cannot be classified, and the request rejects with an `AggregateError` carrying `SUSPENSE_PROBE_FAILED` (both the thrown value and the getter error are kept in `.errors`).

A snapshot carries only durations, never the sender's absolute time. `remainingTtlMs: null` means no time-based expiry. Only the time metadata is directly JSON-encodable; the caller ensures the business `data` is serializable. See `hydrate()` for who accounts for transport time and for the v1 migration note.
`Resource` combines building blocks from `@migaia/lifecycle` and `@migaia/reactive` directly; knowing them helps when diagnosing boundary behaviour:

items: `createGenerationController()` (from `@migaia/lifecycle`): every request calls `begin()` to open a new generation; `refetch()`/`invalidate()`/dependency changes void the old one (`supersede()`), and only a generation for which `isCurrent(token)` is true writes its result into `state`. `dispose()` ends the controller with its `dispose()`.
`createTerminalController()` (from `@migaia/lifecycle`): drives the `Resource`'s own lifetime axis (`open → closing → terminal`); the `disposed` getter reads its `lifecycle === 'terminal'`.

`probeThenable()` / `assimilateCapturedThen()` (from `@migaia/utils/function`): safely detect whether a value thrown by the `fetcher` is a thenable (the Suspense throw-a-Promise pattern), reading `.then` only once so that a hostile getter is not read twice and no exception is swallowed.

`systemScheduler` (from `@migaia/utils/scheduler`) / `snapshotScheduler()` (from `@migaia/lifecycle`): the default and the validation for the `scheduler` option; TTL expiry checks and retry delays go through it rather than the host `setTimeout`/`Date.now`.

`internalRuntimeOf()` / `createTrackedObserver()` (from `@migaia/reactive/extension`): the Resource joins the graph as an `IObserver` and receives only the tracking, suspension, revalidation and idle capabilities bound to itself. Reactive maintains the dependency set; requests, cancellation and resource release remain the Resource's job.

items: A dependency changed but nothing reloaded: check that the reactive read happens before the fetcher's first `await`; reads after an `await` are not tracked. Move them into a `Computed` or read them into local variables first.

The underlying request seems to keep running after `cancel()` or a dependency change: the `fetcher` did not hand `ctx.signal` to I/O that can really be cancelled; `cancel()` only makes the `Resource` ignore the result and cannot stop a request that never received the `signal`.
Reading `state`/`promise` again does not bring the latest data: passive reads start a request only when expired or `idle`, and reading again never forces a refresh; use `refetch()` or `invalidate()`.
A read throws `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`: the `Resource` was `dispose()`d; drop the reference and create a new `Resource`.
A read throws `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE`: calling `peek()` on a legitimate `autoStart: false` idle resource also does this; inspect with `peekState()`, or start work with `promise`/`refetch()`.

`hydrate()`/`initialSnapshot` throws `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`: snapshots usually come from server serialization or persisted storage, and format drift should fail at load time; check how the snapshot is produced and serialized, and confirm `version === 2`, a finite non-negative `ageMs`, and a finite non-negative or `null` `remainingTtlMs`.

After a long idle period, a read seems to have "lost" its dependencies and recomputed: `keepAlive` defaults to `false`; an unobserved resource disconnects upstream but keeps versions and the cache, and the next read checks the dependencies first and does not reload when they are unchanged and fresh. Pass `keepAlive: true` to keep hot data even when nobody watches.

A Suspense throw inside the `fetcher` is not recognized: if the thrown value's `.then` getter itself throws, the result is `SUSPENSE_PROBE_FAILED` rather than a silent retry as an ordinary fetch failure; find out why the value has a throwing getter.

blocks.text: One request reuses one pending Promise across every Suspense wait. After a thenable thrown by the fetcher settles, the work continues through a 0 ms task on the injected scheduler; Suspense waits do not count as retries and have no upper limit. Even when the fetcher keeps throwing thenables that settle at once, cancellation tasks can still run, and `cancel()`/`dispose()` stop further calls.

State type migration: `ResourceStatus.fetching` became `ResourceFetchStatus.fetching`; the former `IResourceStatus` / `IResourceFetchStatus` types are replaced by the key unions `ResourceStatus` / `ResourceFetchStatus` that share their constants' names. The runtime status strings and the data and transport semantics of background refresh are unchanged.

`peekState()` returns the current `IResourceState<T>` without tracking, loading or TTL revalidation. Unlike `peek()`, it returns the state union rather than taking the value out or throwing. `reset()` cancels any pending generation, clears dependency edges and cached data, and leaves this same instance idle and reusable. The old pending Promise rejects immediately with a native `AbortError`, source `@migaia/resource`, code `REQUEST_ABORTED`; reset never reuses a prior generation or token.

`IResourceFetchContext` is the readonly request identity (`signal`, a monotonic `generation`, an opaque `token`). Retries keep that identity; replacement requests receive a new one. Keep request identity separate from the counters used for observation and suspension. Ownership of loaded values and render-version leases belongs to adapters, not to the Resource dependency graph. StoreLight uses these capabilities with one Resource instance, preserving the original `T` and the shared request Promise.

  ttl?: number // 默认 Infinity（永不过期，除非依赖变化/手动刷新）

  initialSnapshot?: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>

blocks.text: 逐项语义与校验：

items: `ttl?: number` —— 成功值的新鲜时长（毫秒）。`0` 与 `Infinity`（默认）表示永不因时间过期，只会因依赖变化/`refetch()`/`invalidate()` 而刷新。非 `Infinity` 时必须是有限非负数，否则抛贴 `INVALID_OPTION` 码的 `RangeError`；`updatedAt + ttl` 运算结果非有限（数值溢出）同样抛 `INVALID_OPTION`。
`autoStart?: boolean` —— 是否在构造函数内立即发起首次请求。默认 `true`。若同时提供了新鲜的 `initialSnapshot`，即使 `autoStart: true` 也不会立即再发一次请求。
`staleWhileRevalidate?: boolean` —— 默认 `false`。为 `true` 时，刷新期间继续展示旧的 `success` 数据（附带 `refreshing: true`），而不是回退到 `pending`。

`retry?: number | (failureCount, error) => boolean` —— 固定次数或自定义判断函数。数字必须是非负整数，否则抛 `INVALID_OPTION`。函数形式在每次失败后被调用一次，用第几次失败（从 1 开始）与错误对象决定是否重试；Suspense 抛出的 thenable 值不计入失败次数（`fetcher` 内部同步抛出一个 thenable 是被当作"需要等待后重跑"处理的，不是一次真实失败）。

`retryDelay?: number | (failureCount, error) => number` —— 固定延迟或按失败次数计算的函数，单位毫秒。数字必须是有限非负数；函数返回非数字时以原生 `TypeError`/`INVALID_OPTION` 拒绝；返回负数/非有限数字则为 `RangeError`/`INVALID_OPTION`。策略抛错或返回非法值时保留触发重试的 fetch 主因，原生策略 Error 尽量原样附码，已有外部身份不改写。
`keepAlive?: boolean` —— 默认 `false`：长时间无人观察 `state` 会在下一个 idle 时机自动休眠（断开上游边、保留依赖版本与缓存），下次读取核对版本；依赖未变且缓存新鲜时继续复用，变更时重拉。设为 `true` 时禁用自动休眠。
`initialSnapshot?: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>` —— SSR/持久化恢复用的初始成功快照；构造期即 `hydrate()`，格式非法抛 `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`（详见快照类型）。

`scheduler?: IScheduler`（`@migaia/utils/scheduler`）—— 时间域与排程来源：TTL/`updatedAt`/`expiresAt`/重试延迟全部走同一个调度器，默认 `@migaia/utils/scheduler` 的 `systemScheduler`（单调时钟）。传入的值必须满足 `{ now(): number; schedule(cb, delayMs): IScheduledTask }` 契约（内部用 `snapshotScheduler` 校验），否则抛 `INVALID_OPTION`；缺宿主能力时该 scheduler 在被调用时才 fail-fast，不会静默降级成微任务。

blocks.text: 逐项语义与校验：

items: `ttl?: number` —— 成功值的新鲜时长（毫秒）。`0` 与 `Infinity`（默认）表示永不因时间过期，只会因依赖变化/`refetch()`/`invalidate()` 而刷新。非 `Infinity` 时必须是有限非负数，否则抛贴 `INVALID_OPTION` 码的 `RangeError`；`updatedAt + ttl` 运算结果非有限（数值溢出）同样抛 `INVALID_OPTION`。
`autoStart?: boolean` —— 是否在构造函数内立即发起首次请求。默认 `true`。若同时提供了新鲜的 `initialSnapshot`，即使 `autoStart: true` 也不会立即再发一次请求。
`staleWhileRevalidate?: boolean` —— 默认 `false`。为 `true` 时，刷新期间继续展示旧的 `success` 数据（附带 `refreshing: true`），而不是回退到 `pending`。

`retry?: number | (failureCount, error) => boolean` —— 固定次数或自定义判断函数。数字必须是非负整数，否则抛 `INVALID_OPTION`。函数形式在每次失败后被调用一次，用第几次失败（从 1 开始）与错误对象决定是否重试；Suspense 抛出的 thenable 值不计入失败次数（`fetcher` 内部同步抛出一个 thenable 是被当作"需要等待后重跑"处理的，不是一次真实失败）。

`retryDelay?: number | (failureCount, error) => number` —— 固定延迟或按失败次数计算的函数，单位毫秒。数字必须是有限非负数；函数返回非数字时以原生 `TypeError`/`INVALID_OPTION` 拒绝；返回负数/非有限数字则为 `RangeError`/`INVALID_OPTION`。策略抛错或返回非法值时保留触发重试的 fetch 主因，原生策略 Error 尽量原样附码，已有外部身份不改写。
`keepAlive?: boolean` —— 默认 `false`：长时间无人观察 `state` 会在下一个 idle 时机自动休眠（断开上游边、保留依赖版本与缓存），下次读取核对版本；依赖未变且缓存新鲜时继续复用，变更时重拉。设为 `true` 时禁用自动休眠。
`initialSnapshot?: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>` —— SSR/持久化恢复用的初始成功快照；构造期即 `hydrate()`，格式非法抛 `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`（详见快照类型）。

`scheduler?: IScheduler`（`@migaia/utils/scheduler`）—— 时间域与排程来源：TTL/`updatedAt`/`expiresAt`/重试延迟全部走同一个调度器，默认 `@migaia/utils/scheduler` 的 `systemScheduler`（单调时钟）。传入的值必须满足 `{ now(): number; schedule(cb, delayMs): IScheduledTask }` 契约（内部用 `snapshotScheduler` 校验），否则抛 `INVALID_OPTION`；缺宿主能力时该 scheduler 在被调用时才 fail-fast，不会静默降级成微任务。

deps: Reactive values the last request read synchronously; a change in any of them schedules a new request. Read-only, for diagnostics.
depVersions: Version of each dependency seen by the last request, used by the reactive runtime to skip refreshes when nothing really changed.
runtime: The runtime passed to the constructor; the resource registers itself there as an observer.
debugName: Label given by the `debugName` option, shown in reactive diagnostics and request error context.
state: Current state as a reactive read: an effect that reads it reruns when the state changes. Reading an expired success value starts a revalidation. Throws `RESOURCE_DISPOSED` after `dispose()`.
promise: Promise of the current request, or a resolved Promise of a fresh cached value. Readers share the latest published request Promise; a reentrant fetcher cannot overwrite a Promise of a newer request. Reading it starts work only when idle or stale.
disposed: `true` after `dispose()`; still readable afterwards, unlike most members.
refreshing: `true` while a background refresh runs and the previous success data stays visible (`staleWhileRevalidate`).
fetchStatus: `fetching` while any request runs, otherwise `idle`; separate from `state.status`.
isStale: `true` when the cached success value is older than `ttl`; `false` for any other state.
observed: `true` while some effect or computed currently reads `state`; without observers and without `keepAlive` the resource drops its upstream dependencies.
read: Suspense-style read with tracking: returns the data on success, throws the pending Promise while loading, and throws the error after failure or cancellation.
The data of the current success state.
peek: Materializes the current state without tracking, starting work or revalidating TTL. Pending throws its Promise; normal `autoStart: false` idle with no Promise throws `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE`. Inspect `peekState()` or explicitly start work first.
peekState: Returns the state without tracking, without starting work and without checking `ttl`.
An `IResourceState` snapshot: branch on `status` (`idle`, `pending`, `success` with `data`, `error` / `cancelled` with `error`).
reset: Cancels the running request, drops cached data and returns to `idle`; the next read starts again.
Nothing; the state is now `idle`.
refetch: Starts a new request even if the cache is fresh, aborting the running one.
Promise of the new request result.
invalidate: Marks the cached data as expired and starts a replacement request at once.
Promise of the replacement request result.
cancel: With an active request, aborts it and pauses passive restarts. Pending becomes `cancelled` (`REQUEST_CANCELLED`); a stale-while-revalidate refresh keeps its success data. Without active work this is a no-op; explicit `refetch()` resumes work.
Nothing; active work is cancelled while cached success data may remain.
dehydrate: Captures a v2 success snapshot with portable durations and unchanged caller-owned data. Only time metadata is directly JSON-encodable: BigInt or cyclic data needs caller serialization. Use safe transport or HTML-context encoding; never insert raw JSON into a script element.
An `IResourceCacheSnapshot`, or `undefined` when the state is not `success`.
hydrate: Replaces the state with a success snapshot produced by `dehydrate()`, cancelling any running request. An expired snapshot is revalidated on the next read. Nothing; the state is now `success`.

Nothing; a refresh is scheduled.
onDependencyDisconnected: The reactive runtime calls this when an input used by the Resource has been disposed and can no longer supply a value. mutate: Replaces the visible data locally (optimistic update, server push, cache write). An `IReactiveComputed` from `@migaia/reactive`; read it through `value` inside effects.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Creates one async data source bound to a reactive runtime. Every request gets a generation; only the result of the newest generation is written to `state`, and replaced requests receive an aborted `signal`. With `autoStart` (default) the first request starts in the constructor unless `initialSnapshot` is fresh.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import Resource from @migaia/resource, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use Resource when its class contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when Resource does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained class example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
fetcher: Function `(context) => value | Promise` that loads the data. `context` comes from the resource for each request: `signal` aborts when the request is replaced, reset, cancelled or disposed; `generation` is the request number; `token` stays the same across retries of one request. Reactive values read synchronously (before the first `await`) become dependencies. Final unclassified fetch failures receive `FETCH_FAILED`; existing external error identity stays intact, and immutable errors or primitive failures remain reachable through `cause`.
runtime: Reactive runtime returned by `createRuntime()` from `@migaia/reactive`; the same runtime must own the signals the fetcher reads and the effects that read `state`. `dispose()` does not dispose it.
A `Resource` instance; invalid options throw `INVALID_OPTION`, an invalid `initialSnapshot` throws `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`.
deps: Reactive values the last request read synchronously; a change in any of them schedules a new request. Read-only, for diagnostics.
depVersions: Version of each dependency seen by the last request, used by the reactive runtime to skip refreshes when nothing really changed.
runtime: The runtime passed to the constructor; the resource registers itself there as an observer.
debugName: Label given by the `debugName` option, shown in reactive diagnostics and request error context.
state: Current state as a reactive read: an effect that reads it reruns when the state changes. Reading an expired success value starts a revalidation. Throws `RESOURCE_DISPOSED` after `dispose()`.
promise: Promise of the current request, or a resolved Promise of a fresh cached value. Readers share the latest published request Promise; a reentrant fetcher cannot overwrite a Promise of a newer request. Reading it starts work only when idle or stale.
disposed: `true` after `dispose()`; still readable afterwards, unlike most members.
refreshing: `true` while a background refresh runs and the previous success data stays visible (`staleWhileRevalidate`).
fetchStatus: `fetching` while any request runs, otherwise `idle`; separate from `state.status`.
isStale: `true` when the cached success value is older than `ttl`; `false` for any other state.
observed: `true` while some effect or computed currently reads `state`; without observers and without `keepAlive` the resource drops its upstream dependencies.
read: Suspense-style read with tracking: returns the data on success, throws the pending Promise while loading, and throws the error after failure or cancellation.
The data of the current success state.
peek: Materializes the current state without tracking, starting work or revalidating TTL. Pending throws its Promise; normal `autoStart: false` idle with no Promise throws `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE`. Inspect `peekState()` or explicitly start work first.
peekState: Returns the state without tracking, without starting work and without checking `ttl`.
An `IResourceState` snapshot: branch on `status` (`idle`, `pending`, `success` with `data`, `error` / `cancelled` with `error`).
reset: Cancels the running request, drops cached data and returns to `idle`; the next read starts again.
Nothing; the state is now `idle`.
refetch: Starts a new request even if the cache is fresh, aborting the running one.
Promise of the new request result.
invalidate: Marks the cached data as expired and starts a replacement request at once.
Promise of the replacement request result.
cancel: With an active request, aborts it and pauses passive restarts. Pending becomes `cancelled` (`REQUEST_CANCELLED`); a stale-while-revalidate refresh keeps its success data. Without active work this is a no-op; explicit `refetch()` resumes work.
Nothing; active work is cancelled while cached success data may remain.
dehydrate: Captures a v2 success snapshot with portable durations and unchanged caller-owned data. Only time metadata is directly JSON-encodable: BigInt or cyclic data needs caller serialization. Use safe transport or HTML-context encoding; never insert raw JSON into a script element.
An `IResourceCacheSnapshot`, or `undefined` when the state is not `success`.
hydrate: Replaces the state with a success snapshot produced by `dehydrate()`, cancelling any running request. An expired snapshot is revalidated on the next read. Durations are rebased to the receiving scheduler; callers add known transport/storage time to `ageMs` and subtract it from finite `remainingTtlMs` (minimum zero). Old v1 snapshots are rejected.
hydrate.snapshot: Snapshot returned by `dehydrate()` (often on the server); malformed snapshots throw `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`.
Nothing; the state is now `success`.
markDirty: The reactive runtime calls this when a value read by the Resource request changes. It schedules a refresh and groups repeated notifications into that scheduled refresh. Application code changes the input, such as userId.value, and lets the runtime send this notification; it does not need to call markDirty().
Nothing; a refresh is scheduled.
onDependencyDisconnected: The reactive runtime calls this when an input used by the Resource has been disposed and can no longer supply a value. It schedules another request even without an ordinary input change. If that request fails while reading the disposed input, the failure becomes visible in the Resource error state. Application code disposes the input and lets the runtime call this method.
Nothing; a forced refresh is scheduled.
mutate: Replaces the visible data locally (optimistic update, server push, cache write). Any in-flight request is superseded so its late result cannot overwrite this value, and a new TTL window starts. An updater receives the current success data or `undefined`; function-typed data must be passed through an updater.
mutate.next: New data, or an `IResourceUpdater` `(previous) => next`; an updater throw leaves the state unchanged.
This resource, for chaining; after `dispose()` it throws `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`.
subscribe: Delivers the current state now and after every change to code that does not run inside the reactive graph (plain scripts, devtools, Node). Subscribing counts as observation, so it can start and keep requests alive. Listener throws are reported through `runtime.reportError` and do not stop delivery.
subscribe.listener: Function `(state) => void` receiving each `IResourceState`; a non-function throws `INVALID_OPTION`.
An idempotent unsubscribe function; `dispose()` unsubscribes automatically.
select: Creates a reactive value derived from the success data; it is `undefined` while the resource is not in `success`, and it is disposed together with the resource.
select.selector: Function `(data) => result`; a non-function throws `INVALID_OPTION`.
An `IReactiveComputed` from `@migaia/reactive`; read it through `value` inside effects.
[Symbol.dispose]: Same as `dispose()`, so a `using` declaration ends the resource when its block exits.
Nothing; the resource is terminal.
dispose: Ends the resource: cancels the request, removes dependencies and subscriptions. Calling it again does nothing; afterwards data reads and operations throw `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`, while `disposed`, `refreshing` and `observed` stay readable. The runtime is not disposed.
debugName: Label shown in reactive diagnostics and in request error context.
Not set: diagnostics show no label.
ttl: Success lifetime in milliseconds; positive finite lifetimes revalidate on an expired read. `0` and `Infinity` disable time expiration, but changed dependencies, including after suspension, still trigger refetching. Must be ≥ 0 or `Infinity`.
`Infinity`: fresh until a dependency changes or `refetch()` is called.
autoStart: Start the first request in the constructor.
`true`: starts immediately unless the initial snapshot is fresh.
staleWhileRevalidate: Keep showing expired success data while the refresh runs (`refreshing` is `true`) instead of switching to `pending`.
`false`: an expired value is replaced by `pending`.
retry: Retry policy after a failure: a non-negative integer of extra attempts, or `(failureCount, error) => boolean` deciding each retry. A Promise thrown for Suspense does not count as a failure. A throwing policy or invalid result yields `INVALID_OPTION`; the triggering fetch failure stays reachable through `cause` or `errors`, and existing external identity is preserved.
`0`: no retry.
retryDelay: Wait before each retry in milliseconds, or `(failureCount, error) => ms` for backoff. Throwing callbacks or invalid results retain the fetch failure in `cause` or `errors`; policy errors receive `INVALID_OPTION` unless already classified externally.
`0`: retry immediately.
Pass a function when the server is overloaded or rate limited: immediate retries add load at the worst moment. `failureCount` starts at 1, so `1000 * 2 ** (failureCount - 1)` waits 1 s, 2 s, 4 s. You can also read `error` and wait longer for a 429 than for a network error. A plain number is enough when failures are short network blips.
keepAlive: Keep upstream dependencies connected while nothing reads `state`, so changes are still tracked.
`false`: unobserved resources disconnect upstream.
initialSnapshot: Success snapshot from `dehydrate()` (server rendering or persistence) used as the initial state; it is revalidated when expired.
Not set: start from `idle`.
scheduler: Clock and timers for `ttl`, `updatedAt`, `expiresAt` and retry delays; inject a manual scheduler in tests.
`systemScheduler` from `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.

blocks.text: 用户点了“取消导出”，界面却弹出“导出失败”，因为取消和失败走进了同一个 `catch`。
手写的状态通常只有“加载中、成功、失败”三种，取消只能塞进“失败”，再靠比较错误信息字符串来区分。
`cancel()` 把还在等待的请求变成 `cancelled` 状态，`state.error` 是原生 `AbortError`。资源本身没有被释放，之后调用 `refetch()` 可以重新开始。
输出：

blocks.code:
状态：cancelled
原因：AbortError
第 2 次导出完成

blocks.text: 取消后状态是 `cancelled`，原因是 `AbortError`；随后 `refetch()` 正常完成，输出“第 2 次导出完成”。
`cancelled` 是单独的状态，界面可以按 `ResourceStatus.cancelled` 显示“已取消”。取消后再读取 `state` 不会自动重启请求，只有显式调用 `refetch()` 才会。

函数式构建 `Resource`。`setup` 只同步执行一次，拿到 `{ runtime, scheduler, signal, debugName, onDispose }`，返回 fetcher；数据类型从 fetcher 推导。`options` 就是 `IResourceOptions` 加上可选的 `runtime`（默认 `@migaia/reactive` 的 `defaultRuntime`）。

items: `onDispose` 注册的清理在 `dispose()` 时按注册的逆序执行，`signal` 同时中止。
`setup` 抛错、返回值不是函数（`RESOURCE_SETUP_INVALID`）或选项非法时，先中止 `signal`、逆序执行已注册清理，再重抛原始错误；清理失败挂在 `errors` 上。
`setup` 返回后再调用 `onDispose` 会抛 `RESOURCE_SETUP_CLOSED`，避免泄漏。

blocks.text: 配合 `ConfigOwner.fromAsync` 得到配置资源：

blocks.code: const config = createResource(() => ({ signal }) => ConfigOwner.fromAsync(fetch(url, { signal }).then((r) => r.text())))

type IResourceOptions<T = unknown> = {
  debugName?: string
  ttl?: number // 默认 Infinity（永不过期，除非依赖变化/手动刷新）
  autoStart?: boolean // 默认 true
  staleWhileRevalidate?: boolean // 默认 false
  retry?: IResourceRetryPolicy // 默认 0（不重试）
  retryDelay?: number | ((failureCount: number, error: unknown) => number) // 默认 0
  keepAlive?: boolean // 默认 false
  initialSnapshot?: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>
  scheduler?: IScheduler // 默认 @migaia/utils/scheduler 的 systemScheduler
}

type IResourceRetryPolicy = number | ((failureCount: number, error: unknown) => boolean)

blocks.text: 逐项语义与校验：

items: `ttl?: number` —— 成功值的新鲜时长（毫秒）。`0` 与 `Infinity`（默认）表示永不因时间过期，只会因依赖变化/`refetch()`/`invalidate()` 而刷新。非 `Infinity` 时必须是有限非负数，否则抛贴 `INVALID_OPTION` 码的 `RangeError`；`updatedAt + ttl` 运算结果非有限（数值溢出）同样抛 `INVALID_OPTION`。
`autoStart?: boolean` —— 是否在构造函数内立即发起首次请求。默认 `true`。若同时提供了新鲜的 `initialSnapshot`，即使 `autoStart: true` 也不会立即再发一次请求。
`staleWhileRevalidate?: boolean` —— 默认 `false`。为 `true` 时，刷新期间继续展示旧的 `success` 数据（附带 `refreshing: true`），而不是回退到 `pending`。

`retry?: number | (failureCount, error) => boolean` —— 固定次数或自定义判断函数。数字必须是非负整数，否则抛 `INVALID_OPTION`。函数形式在每次失败后被调用一次，用第几次失败（从 1 开始）与错误对象决定是否重试；Suspense 抛出的 thenable 值不计入失败次数（`fetcher` 内部同步抛出一个 thenable 是被当作"需要等待后重跑"处理的，不是一次真实失败）。

`retryDelay?: number | (failureCount, error) => number` —— 固定延迟或按失败次数计算的函数，单位毫秒。数字必须是有限非负数；函数返回非数字时以原生 `TypeError`/`INVALID_OPTION` 拒绝；返回负数/非有限数字则为 `RangeError`/`INVALID_OPTION`。策略抛错或返回非法值时保留触发重试的 fetch 主因，原生策略 Error 尽量原样附码，已有外部身份不改写。
`keepAlive?: boolean` —— 默认 `false`：长时间无人观察 `state` 会在下一个 idle 时机自动休眠（断开上游边、保留依赖版本与缓存），下次读取核对版本；依赖未变且缓存新鲜时继续复用，变更时重拉。设为 `true` 时禁用自动休眠。
`initialSnapshot?: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>` —— SSR/持久化恢复用的初始成功快照；构造期即 `hydrate()`，格式非法抛 `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`（详见快照类型）。

`scheduler?: IScheduler`（`@migaia/utils/scheduler`）—— 时间域与排程来源：TTL/`updatedAt`/`expiresAt`/重试延迟全部走同一个调度器，默认 `@migaia/utils/scheduler` 的 `systemScheduler`（单调时钟）。传入的值必须满足 `{ now(): number; schedule(cb, delayMs): IScheduledTask }` 契约（内部用 `snapshotScheduler` 校验），否则抛 `INVALID_OPTION`；缺宿主能力时该 scheduler 在被调用时才 fail-fast，不会静默降级成微任务。

guidance.heading: 底层依赖：lifecycle 原语的使用方式

blocks.text: `Resource` 内部直接组合 `@migaia/lifecycle` 与 `@migaia/reactive` 的原语，理解这层有助于诊断边界行为：

items: `createGenerationController()`（来自 `@migaia/lifecycle`）——每次发起请求都调用 `begin()` 开一代新请求；`refetch()`/`invalidate()`/依赖变化都会使旧一代失效（`supersede()`），只有 `isCurrent(token)` 为真的那一代结果才会写入 `state`。`dispose()` 时调用其 `dispose()` 终结控制器。
`createTerminalController()`（来自 `@migaia/lifecycle`）——驱动 `Resource` 自身的容器存活轴（`open → closing → terminal`）；`disposed` getter 直接读它的 `lifecycle === 'terminal'`。
`probeThenable()` / `assimilateCapturedThen()`（来自 `@migaia/utils/function`）——用于安全探测 `fetcher` 同步抛出的值是否是 thenable（Suspense 抛 Promise 模式），只读一次 `.then`，避免 hostile getter 被读取两次或异常被吞掉。
`systemScheduler`（来自 `@migaia/utils/scheduler`）/ `snapshotScheduler()`（来自 `@migaia/lifecycle`）——`scheduler` 选项的默认值与校验函数；TTL 到期判定、重试延迟计时都通过它，不直接使用宿主 `setTimeout`/`Date.now`。

guidance.id: 高阶组合示例-1-suspense-兼容读取-error-boundary
guidance.heading: 高阶组合示例 · 1. Suspense 兼容读取 + Error Boundary

blocks.text: 1. 依赖追踪只认第一个 `await` 之前的同步读取。 `await` 之后再读响应式值不会被追踪；需要时先把值读进局部变量，或者把读取挪进一个 `Computed`。 2. 请求函数要把 `signal` 交给真正可取消的 I/O（例如 `fetch(url, { signal })`）。否则取消只是让 `Resource` 忽略这次结果，底层请求仍会跑完。 3. `refetch()` 总是发起新请求；被动读取（`state`、`promise`、`read()`）只在 `idle` 或数据过期时才发起。 想强制刷新就调用 `refetch()` 或 `invalidate()`。 4. 不再使用时要调用 `dispose()`，否则依赖登记和进行中的请求会一直留着。释放后读取数据和发起请求都抛 `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`；`disposed`、`refreshing`、`observed` 仍可读，`markDirty()`、`onDependencyDisconnected()` 和再次 `dispose()` 是安全的空操作。`dispose()` 不会释放传入的 `runtime`。 5. 默认 `keepAlive: false`。 没人读取 `state` 时，`Resource` 会和上游断开但保留依赖版本与缓存；下次读取时依赖没变且缓存有效就复用原值和 Promise，依赖变了就重新请求。需要“没人看也保持连接”时传 `keepAlive: true`。 6. `cancel()` 之后被动读取不会自动重启。 正在加载的请求被取消后状态是 `cancelled`；后台刷新被取消时保留旧数据并清除 `refreshing`。只有显式 `refetch()` 会重新开始。

`Resource` 自己产生的错误带 `source === RESOURCE_SOURCE`（`@migaia/resource`）和 `ResourceErrorCode` 里的 `code`。已经有完整 `source`/`code` 的外部错误保持原样；没有分类的加载失败在重试结束后附加 `FETCH_FAILED`，原生错误保持原类型，不可修改的错误保留在 `cause` 链上。重试策略本身出错时附加 `INVALID_OPTION`，触发它的加载错误仍可从错误链找到。取消和释放产生的错误是原生 `DOMException`（`name === 'AbortError'`），按 `error.name` 判断即可。

symbols.purpose: Table of the stable error codes of this package. Each key names one failure; the values are the strings found on `error.code`.
symbols.core:
resourceDisposed: `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`: a member was used after `dispose()`; create a new resource.
requestAborted: `REQUEST_ABORTED`: Resource-initiated cancellation uses the same native AbortError as its signal reason and rejection. Lifecycle replacement can supply a different signal reason, retained on the `cause` of the Resource AbortError.
requestCancelled: `REQUEST_CANCELLED`: the `AbortError` stored in the `cancelled` state after `cancel()`.
cancellationCleanupFailed: `CANCELLATION_CLEANUP_FAILED`: a timer or listener could not be cleaned after cancellation; the resource still counts as cancelled.
noActivePromise: `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE`: no request Promise is available, including a valid `autoStart: false` idle `peek()`; inspect `peekState()` or explicitly start a request.
invalidSnapshot: `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`: snapshot version is not `2`, durations are negative/non-finite (only remaining lifetime permits `null`), or rebased local timestamps overflow. Getter failures retain their cause.
invalidOption: `INVALID_OPTION`: an option such as `ttl`, `retry` or `retryDelay` is invalid; fix the options.
fetchFailed: `FETCH_FAILED`: final unclassified fetch failure after retries. Native errors keep identity when writable; immutable errors and primitive values stay reachable through `cause`. Existing foreign source/code is preserved.
setupInvalid: `RESOURCE_SETUP_INVALID`: `createResource()` got a non-function setup, or setup returned a non-function; registered cleanups already ran. Return a fetcher from setup.
setupClosed: `RESOURCE_SETUP_CLOSED`: `onDispose()` was called after setup returned, for example from an async callback; register cleanups synchronously during setup.
suspenseProbeFailed: `SUSPENSE_PROBE_FAILED`: a value thrown by the fetcher has a throwing `then` getter; both errors are kept in `errors`.

sections.content:
resourceDisposed: `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`: a member was used after `dispose()`; create a new resource.
requestAborted: `REQUEST_ABORTED`: Resource-initiated cancellation uses the same native AbortError as its signal reason and rejection. Lifecycle replacement can supply a different signal reason, retained on the `cause` of the Resource AbortError.
requestCancelled: `REQUEST_CANCELLED`: the `AbortError` stored in the `cancelled` state after `cancel()`.
cancellationCleanupFailed: `CANCELLATION_CLEANUP_FAILED`: a timer or listener could not be cleaned after cancellation; the resource still counts as cancelled.
noActivePromise: `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE`: no request Promise is available, including a valid `autoStart: false` idle `peek()`; inspect `peekState()` or explicitly start a request.
invalidSnapshot: `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`: snapshot version is not `2`, durations are negative/non-finite (only remaining lifetime permits `null`), or rebased local timestamps overflow. Getter failures retain their cause.
invalidOption: `INVALID_OPTION`: an option such as `ttl`, `retry` or `retryDelay` is invalid; fix the options.
fetchFailed: `FETCH_FAILED`: final unclassified fetch failure after retries. Native errors keep identity when writable; immutable errors and primitive values stay reachable through `cause`. Existing foreign source/code is preserved.
setupInvalid: `RESOURCE_SETUP_INVALID`: `createResource()` got a non-function setup, or setup returned a non-function; registered cleanups already ran. Return a fetcher from setup.
setupClosed: `RESOURCE_SETUP_CLOSED`: `onDispose()` was called after setup returned, for example from an async callback; register cleanups synchronously during setup.
suspenseProbeFailed: `SUSPENSE_PROBE_FAILED`: a value thrown by the fetcher has a throwing `then` getter; both errors are kept in `errors`.

blocks.code: import { RESOURCE_SOURCE, ResourceErrorCode, type IResourceErrorCode } from '@migaia/resource'

blocks.text: 稳定错误码表，9 个码，唯一声明处 `src/error-code.ts`，包自身错误的 `source` 为 `'@migaia/resource'`；已有完整外部身份的错误保留原包身份。 `RESOURCE_SOURCE` 导出这个稳定 source，跨包分类错误时应比较它与 `ResourceErrorCode`，不要复制字符串字面量。

rows: 在已 `dispose()` 的 `Resource` 上调用任意读取/操作方法
请求停止时的原生 AbortError；Resource 主动取消时与 signal.reason 同一，lifecycle replacement reason 保留在 cause
调用方显式 `cancel()` 导致当前 pending 请求被取消，`state` 落入 `cancelled` 所携带的 `DOMException`
请求取消已完成状态收敛，但取消期间的 timer/listener cleanup 失败
读取 `promise`，或在 `pending`/`idle` 状态下调用 `read()`/`peek()` 时，没有正在进行或已缓存的 Promise 可返回
非 v2 快照、负/非有限时长（remaining 可为 null）、本地重建时间戳溢出或 getter 失败
构造/调用时传入的选项（`ttl`、`retry`、`retryDelay`、`scheduler` 等）不满足取值要求
`fetcher` 抛出用于 Suspense 的值，但探测其 `.then` 时 getter 本身抛错，无法判定是否为 thenable
重试耗尽后的未分类 fetch 失败；原生错误尽量保留身份，冻结错误/非 Error 值保留在 cause，已有外部身份不改写

blocks.text: `requestAborted`/`requestCancelled` 抛出/落入状态的值始终是原生 `DOMException`（`name === 'AbortError'`），调用方通常按 `error.name === 'AbortError'` 判定并静默处理，而不是当作真实失败；`code` 只作为附加字段挂上，不改变类型。调用方应始终以 `error.code === ResourceErrorCode.xxx` 判别，不要硬编码码值字符串。

`Resource` 自己产生的错误带 `source === RESOURCE_SOURCE`（`@migaia/resource`）和 `ResourceErrorCode` 里的 `code`。已经有完整 `source`/`code` 的外部错误保持原样；没有分类的加载失败在重试结束后附加 `FETCH_FAILED`，原生错误保持原类型，不可修改的错误保留在 `cause` 链上。重试策略本身出错时附加 `INVALID_OPTION`，触发它的加载错误仍可从错误链找到。取消和释放产生的错误是原生 `DOMException`（`name === 'AbortError'`），按 `error.name` 判断即可。

guidance.heading: 取消后显示已取消而不是错误

blocks.text: 用户点了“取消导出”，界面却弹出“导出失败”，因为取消和失败走进了同一个 `catch`。
手写的状态通常只有“加载中、成功、失败”三种，取消只能塞进“失败”，再靠比较错误信息字符串来区分。
`cancel()` 把还在等待的请求变成 `cancelled` 状态，`state.error` 是原生 `AbortError`。资源本身没有被释放，之后调用 `refetch()` 可以重新开始。
输出：

blocks.code:
状态：cancelled
原因：AbortError
第 2 次导出完成

blocks.text: 取消后状态是 `cancelled`，原因是 `AbortError`；随后 `refetch()` 正常完成，输出“第 2 次导出完成”。
`cancelled` 是单独的状态，界面可以按 `ResourceStatus.cancelled` 显示“已取消”。取消后再读取 `state` 不会自动重启请求，只有显式调用 `refetch()` 才会。
